trajectory_summary: The call opens cold with the customer stating outright that she isn't ready and has multiple open variables (pending home inspection, planned addition, unknown roof age) — a legitimate not-yet-qualified scenario, not a hard objection. The rep correctly avoids pushing a booking, but then does almost nothing structured with the call: no bill or usage question, no locked callback date, and a bundle/roofing mention that goes nowhere before the call drifts into unrelated small talk about Utah and South Carolina.
outcome_dispute: This is not a true disqualification — the customer has real interest and gave the rep a usable timeline (May closing) — but it also isn't a booked or tentative appointment. The right tag is callback, and even that is weak because no specific date or time was fixed, only 'in a couple weeks.'

primary_coaching_focus.topic: cross-sell bridge on a live signal
primary_coaching_focus.quote: So is it better to go ahead and have a roof, replaced, or is it better to wait and do that at the same time you're gonna install panels?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer handed the rep a direct, unprompted roofing question — the schema's highest-value cross-sell trigger — and the rep gave a generic answer instead of naming Ion's in-house bundle option and capturing roof detail on the spot. This is the single highest-leverage moment in the call and it was walked past.
